hook.line: A student's second account hit six digits days after the SEO class (paraphrased, Taglish).
hook.visual: Creator cut out at bottom right over a black screenshot of a student's message and a sales dashboard, with word-by-word captions.

beats.what: Student testimonial screenshot behind her face: second account, sales dashboard, long thank-you message
Announces the class runs from January to December 2026
First cut after 39 s of one continuous take, same testimonial background
Background switches to her community chat answering a question about the class length and templates
Background becomes a 'How to join the classes' 3-step list (tap Subscription, pay monthly, start learning)
Her profile with the Subscribe button shown behind her, offering a first-time discount
Ends laughing over the join steps

why_it_works: Opens on a student's proof (a dashboard and a thank-you message) instead of a claim, so the result sells the class before she says what it is
The background changes job with the script: proof, then FAQ answer, then the join steps, so the face never needs cuts to show progress
The join steps are written as a numbered list on screen, so the sales part is skimmable for anyone who stayed
weaknesses: Two minutes with almost no cuts (first cut at 39 s, median shot 7.8 s); energy rests entirely on her delivery
Rambling middle with repeated lines; the pitch could be half as long
The testimonial text is too small to read without pausing
for_robert: Swap the green-screen background to match each part of the script (proof screenshot, then FAQ, then numbered steps); Fred can 'pin up' each new background, but avoid her long uncut stretches.
